verse: Above all, love each other deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.
with_kids: Ask your kids: what does it mean to love someone deeply? Can you think of a time someone loved you that way?

verse: Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.
with_kids: Talk about a time your family had to forgive each other. What made it easier?

verse: Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.
with_kids: Ask: what is something that worries you? Let's tell God about it together right now.

verse: Do everything in love.
with_kids: It's only four words — see if everyone can say it from memory by dinner.

verse: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, who does not change like shifting shadows.
with_kids: Go around the table: what is one good gift you are thankful for today?

verse: For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.
with_kids: This one is worth slowing down on. Read it twice and ask: what does it tell us about how God feels about us?

verse: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his love endures forever.
with_kids: Make it a game: take turns naming something you are grateful for. Keep going until you run out.

verse: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up.
with_kids: Ask: what does it mean to be humble? Is that the same as being weak?

verse: I can do all this through him who gives me strength.
with_kids: Ask each person: what is something hard you are facing right now? Say this verse together over it.

verse: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
with_kids: Ask: what does it mean that Jesus never changes? Why is that good news?

verse: Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from telling lies.
with_kids: Talk about why words matter. Can you think of a time a kind word made a real difference?

verse: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
with_kids: Read it slowly and ask: which of these is hardest for you — patient, kind, not envying, not boasting?

verse: May these words of my mouth and this meditation of my heart be pleasing in your sight, LORD, my Rock and my Redeemer.
with_kids: Try praying this verse together as your dinner prayer tonight.

verse: No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to mankind. And God is faithful; he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, he will also provide a way out so that you can endure it.
with_kids: This is a longer one — take it in pieces. Talk about what the 'way out' might look like in real life.

verse: Open my eyes that I may see wonderful things in your law.
with_kids: Ask: what is something in the Bible that surprised you or that you never noticed before?

verse: Pray continually.
with_kids: Two words — the shortest verse in the challenge. What do you think it means to pray continually?

review_prompt: Practice A–P using only the letters. Go through the alphabet, say the opening word, then try the full verse. No peeking.

verse: Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!
with_kids: Ask: what does rejoice mean? What is something that makes you want to celebrate God today?

verse: Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
with_kids: Ask: what kinds of things crowd your mind during the day? What would it look like to set your mind on something better?

verse: Trust in the LORD with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding;
with_kids: Ask: when is it hardest to trust God instead of figuring things out yourself?

review_prompt: Practice A–J from memory. Say the opening word, then the full verse. These are the ones you learned first — see how solid they feel now.
Practice K–T, skipping Q. All of these are verses — go through each one from the opening word.

verse: When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.
with_kids: Short and powerful. Ask: what is something that scares you? Say this verse over it together.

review_prompt: Choose the three verses that won't stick. Read it, cover it, recite it, repeat. Flag the ones that need more time so your daily strip keeps bringing them back.

verse: Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path.
with_kids: Ask: what does it mean that the Bible is a lamp? What does a lamp actually do for you?

review_title: 21 verses to carry in your heart.
review_prompt: Recite all 21 verses from memory. Start with A and go straight through to Y. Then celebrate — you did the whole thing.
